frequency_question: How often are federal administrative de-recognition proceedings successfully initiated, reviewed, and finalized within a sub-three-month (78-day) timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes any formal administrative agency action aiming to strip an institutional or programmatic accreditor of its federal recognition status. Excludes voluntary relinquishments and routine 5-year renewal reviews that proceed on normal multi-year schedules.

cases.name: ACICS Final Appeals and Closure Actions

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 major contested de-recognition or review cycles examined; all required a minimum of 1 to 6 years due to statutory notice and comment requirements alone.
known_gaps: Minor advisory opinions or emergency extensions are excluded as they do not constitute final revocations.
skeleton: Administrative law procedures require statutory notice, advisory committee review (NACIQI), public comment periods, panel hearings, and secretarial review.
multiplier: 0 historical instances where the entire statutory due process chain of a major accreditor de-recognition was completed within 78 days out of 4 total major contested proceedings.
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act and Higher Education Act statutory notice and hearing timelines are fixed by federal law and do not change absent major legislation.
